{{Quote|This Advozse is a disease-carrying parasite, against whom the Imperial immune system has yet to build a reliable defense—an amoral magnet that confuses the human moral compass.|From the notes of Andressa Divo|<ref name="Scum and Villainy Case Files" />}}
'''Bom Vimdin''' was a widely disliked [[Advozse]] who worked as a [[mercenary]], [[smuggler]], and [[black market]]eer. He earned a reputation for working with corrupt officials, providing illicit goods to [[Imperial officer]]s, and became wanted by the [[Galactic Empire]]. In [[1 BBY]], the Empire held him [[prisoner]] on board its [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station|Death Star]] [[superweapon]], but he managed to escape from his [[Prison|cell]] using an [[Bomb|explosive device]].

After escaping, he spent [[time]] in [[Chalmun's Spaceport Cantina]] in the [[spaceport]] of [[Mos Eisley]] on the [[planet]] [[Tatooine]], sitting at a table with fellow patrons [[Hem Dazon]], [[Pons Limbic]], [[Braconnor Bakiska]], and [[Arleil Schous]]. He was later present in the [[cantina]] again when the [[bounty hunter]] [[Boba Fett]] questioned the patrons there for information on local [[moisture farmer]] [[Luke Skywalker]]. [[New Republic]] [[Law enforcement agency|police]] [[commissioner]] [[Exantor Divo]] later wrote about Vimdin in his [[book]], ''[[Scum and Villainy: Case Files on the Galaxy's Most Notorious]]''.

==Biography==
===Wanted by the Empire===
{{Quote|While it is without question the Imperial officials on the receiving end of a graft should be subject to the harshest response the ISB can muster, we cannot diminish the role that such tempters as Vimdin play.|From the notes of Andressa Divo|<ref name="Scum and Villainy Case Files" />}}
[[File:Bom_Vimdin_escapes.png|thumb|right|300px|Bom Vimdin escaped from the Death Star.]]
[[Reproduction|Born]] around [[29 BBY]]<ref name="Scum&Villany Dates" /> on the [[planet]] [[Riflor]],<ref name="Topps" /> Bom Vimdin was an [[Advozse]] [[mercenary]]<ref name="AEYNTK" /> who became one of the most successful [[smuggler]]s and [[black market]]eers operating in the [[Outer Rim Territories]], selling [[Imperial officer]]s illicit substances and entertainment that was not in keeping with [[Galactic Empire|Imperial]] codes of conduct. By [[1 BBY|7977.44.3 C.R.C.]], he was wanted for crimes against the Galactic Empire—including collusion, bribery, [[Thief|theft]], and conspiracy<ref name="Scum and Villainy Case Files" />—even though he indirectly supported the Imperials.<ref name="Topps" />

[[Imperial Security Bureau]] [[Agent]] [[Andressa Divo]] included a mention of Vimdin in her notes, describing him as a "[[disease]]-carrying [[parasite]]" and "amoral [[magnet]]" who confused the [[human]] moral compass and played an important role in tempting Imperial officials to begin taking bribes. She also noted that the Empire had yet to develop a reliable defense against criminals like Vimdin.<ref name="Scum and Villainy Case Files" />

In 1 [['ABY-BBY' dating system|BBY]],<ref name="Date note">{{BountyHuntDate}}</ref> he ended up as a [[prisoner]] of the Empire and was held in a [[Prison|cell]] on board the [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station|Death Star]] [[superweapon]]. Vimdin managed to get hold of an [[Bomb|explosive device]] and used it to blow a hole in the side of his cell, allowing him to escape into the neighboring corridor and flee from pursuing [[stormtrooper]]s. Soon after escaping from the [[Death Star]], Vimdin was present at the bar of [[Chalmun's Spaceport Cantina]] in the [[Mos Eisley]] [[spaceport]] on the planet [[Tatooine]] when the [[bounty hunter]] [[Bossk'wassak'Cradossk|Bossk]] searched for the rogue Imperial [[astromech droid]] [[261]] there.<ref name="BH">''[[Bounty Hunt]]''</ref>

===Cantina criminal===
[[File:LimbicVimdin-2015StarWars5.png|thumb|left|250px|Vimdin witnessed Boba Fett's search for information on Luke Skywalker.]]
Shortly before the [[Battle of Yavin]]<ref name="ANH" /> in 1 BBY,<ref name="Date note" /> Vimdin was present in the [[cantina]] again and sat at a booth table in one of the establishment's backrooms<ref name="CompleteLocations">''[[Star Wars: Complete Locations, New Edition]]''</ref> with the [[Arcona]] [[Hem Dazon]], the [[Siniteen]] [[Pons Limbic]], the [[Stennes Shifter]] [[Braconnor Bakiska]], and the [[Defel]] [[Arleil Schous]].<ref name="AEYNTK" /> While the group sat together, [[Jedi Master]] [[Obi-Wan Kenobi]] and local [[moisture farmer]] [[Luke Skywalker]] entered the establishment looking for a [[pilot]] to take them to the planet [[Alderaan]].<ref name="ANH" /> Dazon, Bakiska, and Vimdin were still sitting in the booth with several other patrons when Kenobi and Skywalker came into conflict with the thugs [[Doctor]] [[Cornelius Evazan]] and [[Ponda Baba]] at the cantina's bar.<ref name="CompleteLocations" />

Following the Battle of Yavin,<ref name="SW5">[[Star Wars (2015) 5|''Star Wars'' (2015) 5]]</ref> in [[0 ABY]],<ref name="ComicDate">''[[Star Wars: Timelines]]'' dates the events of [[Star Wars (2015) 5|''Star Wars'' (2015) 5]] to [[0 ABY]].</ref> Vimdin and Limbic were both again present in Chalmun's Spaceport Cantina when the [[bounty]] hunter [[Boba Fett]] entered seeking the identity of Skywalker. The pair stood silently as part of a crowd while Fett questioned them until [[Unidentified six-armed alien|one]] of the other patrons challenged him. Fett defeated the patron and eventually got the information he sought by [[Torture|interrogating]] a [[Unidentified moisture farmer (Chalmun's Cantina)|human]] who tried to flee the bar.<ref name="SW5" />

===Legacy===
{{Quote|Bom Vimdin was one of the most successful Outer Rim smugglers and black marketeers.|From the notations of Exantor Divo, ''Scum and Villainy: Case Files on the Galaxy's Most Notorious''|<ref name="Scum and Villainy Case Files" />}}
During the [[New Republic Era]], [[New Republic]] [[Law enforcement agency|police]] [[commissioner]] [[Exantor Divo]], son of Andressa, wrote about Vimdin in his [[book]], ''[[Scum and Villainy: Case Files on the Galaxy's Most Notorious]]'',<ref name="Scum and Villainy Case Files" /> which was published in [[34 ABY]]<ref name="PublishDate">{{ScumAndVillainyDate}}</ref> and detailed the experiences of three generations of law enforcement officials in his [[Divo family|family]]. Divo included his [[Parent|mother's]] notes and the criminal's Imperial wanted [[Painting|poster]] in the book, writing about Vimdin as an example of the opportunists who tempted Imperial [[officer]]s who had been given difficult postings.<ref name="Scum and Villainy Case Files" />

==Personality and traits==
{{Quote|He had a keen eye for Imperials on the edge, and a willing-ness ''[sic]'' to risk contact with Imperial officials. Vimdin often sold illicit substances and entertainments not keeping within the codes of Imperial conduct.|From the notations of Exantor Divo|<ref name="Scum and Villainy Case Files" />}}
[[File:Bom_Vimdin_mugshot_SaV.png|thumb|right|300px|Bom Vimdin's mugshot]]
Bom Vimdin was a gloomy loner with a sour face and personality who obsessed over his [[Galactic Credit Standard|credit]] balance and was universally disliked.<ref name="AEYNTK" /> A cynical individual, he kept mainly to himself and distrusted even those who enlisted his services.<ref name="Topps" /> He was an opportunist with a keen [[eye]] for Imperials on the edge and was willing to risk contacting them,<ref name="Scum and Villainy Case Files" /> earning him a reputation for working with corrupt officials.<ref name="FC">{{ForceCollection|Bom Vimdin|star=1}}</ref> An Advozse with [[Color|pink]] skin and black eyes,<ref name="ANH" /> he despised the rest of his [[species]].<ref name="CVD">''[[Star Wars: The Complete Visual Dictionary, New Edition]]''</ref> He stood 1.8 [[meter]]s tall.<ref name="Scum and Villainy Case Files" />

==Skills and abilities==
Vimdin had above average fighting ability and average speed, strength, and intelligence. He had extremely low [[diplomat]]ic skills and was not [[Force-sensitive]].<ref name="Topps" />

==Equipment==
Bom Vimdin wore a brown [[jerkin]] with metal spikes over a white [[Clothing|shirt]]<ref name="ANH" /> and black pants. He also wore gray [[glove]]s, brown [[boot]]s,<ref name="BH" /> and a brown neckerchief.<ref name="ANH" /> In his wanted poster, he wore a brown shirt.<ref name="Scum and Villainy Case Files" />

==Behind the scenes==
===Film appearance===
[[File:DazonPuppet.png|thumb|left|300px|Bom Vimdin was added during supplemental filming at in Dovington's Hollywood studio.]]
Bom Vimdin first appeared in the [[1977]] [[original trilogy]] film, [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''Star Wars'': Episode IV ''A New Hope'']].<ref name="ANH" /> His scene was added to the film during a series of supplemental shots filmed for the cantina sequence on a sound stage in Dovington's Hollywood studio between [[January 24]]–[[January 25|25]], 1977.<ref name="MakingOf">''[[The Making of Star Wars: The Definitive Story Behind the Original Film]]''</ref> The character was likely portrayed by [[Penny McCarthy]] according to [[Pablo Hidalgo]] and [[Tom Spina]].<ref name="Archeology">{{YouTube|video=ElyMaaAFLKU|text=The Star Wars Cantina PT. 2 | Full Panel #indianacomicconvention #tomspinadesigns #starwarshistory|channel=@FanXComicConventions|name=FanX Comic Conventions|date=2025-05-03}}</ref>

Vimdin's mask was made by [[Rob Bottin]] when he was a child and called "the Martian." He brought it in to be used on the film and they bought the mould, making a copy to use in the film.<ref name="Archeology" /> Vimdin's costume was provided by creature designer [[Rick Baker]] and, on set, the character was known as "[[Wikipedia:Don Rickles|Don Rickles]]" due to his similarity in appearance to the famous [[Wikipedia:Las Vegas|Vegas]] insult-comic.<ref name="SheddingLight">{{SWArchive|url=episode-iv/bts/article/f20030502/index.html|text=Cantina Roll-Call: Shedding Light on Some Alien Aliases|int=Cantina Roll-Call: Shedding Light on Some Alien Aliases}}</ref>

===Other media and naming===
[[File:BomVimdin-GoH.png|thumb|right|300px|Unused concept art of Bom Vimdin made for ''Star Wars: Galaxy of Heroes'']]
In ''[[Star Wars Workbook: Kindergarten Writing & ABCs]]'', a [[2014]] entry in the ''[[Star Wars Workbooks]]'' series, Vimdin is depicted in one of the hypothetical exercises as sitting with a [[Gotal]] while watching the [[Jedi]] [[Aayla Secura]] sing.<ref name="ABC">''[[Star Wars Workbook: Kindergarten Writing & ABCs]]''</ref> Vimdin appeared in [[Jeffrey Brown]]'s [[2021]] non-[[canon]] children's book, ''[[A Vader Family Sithmas]]'', in which he can be seen listening to [[Figrin D'an and the Modal Nodes]] playing holiday [[music]] at Chalmun's Spaceport Cantina.<ref name="Sithmas">''[[A Vader Family Sithmas]]''</ref> Concept art of Vimdim was created for the [[Star Wars video games|video game]] ''[[Star Wars: Galaxy of Heroes]]'' by senior artist [[Paul Martin]];<ref name="ArtStation">{{ArtStation|username=morepaul|url=artwork/B3XwaA|name=[[Paul Martin]]|text=Star Wars Galaxy of Heroes - Character Concepts|date=2021}}</ref> however, he is yet to appear in the game itself.<ref name="GoH">''[[Star Wars: Galaxy of Heroes]]''</ref>

In the new ''[[Star Wars]]'' canon, Vimdin was first named in the mobile card game ''[[Star Wars: Force Collection]]'',<ref name="FC" /> which initially launched in [[2013]]. Although the launch of ''Force Collection'' predates<ref name="Force Collection release">{{SW|url=news/announcing-star-wars-force-collection|text=Announcing Star Wars: Force Collection|nolive=1}}</ref> the ''Star Wars'' canon reset of 2014,<ref name="Legends">{{SW|url=news/the-legendary-star-wars-expanded-universe-turns-a-new-page|text=The Legendary Star Wars Expanded Universe Turns a New Page}}</ref> [[Lucasfilm Story Group]] member [[Leland Chee]] confirmed that the game was kept updated to fit with canon.<ref name="Twitter">{{Twitter|holocronkeeper|status/846807700482666496|[[Leland Chee]]|quote=I'm not gonna go through the trouble of changing them and I don't have any reason to believe currently that anyone would. […] On the off-chance that we DID have a current need to change any of these, we would have for Force Collection.|archivefile=File:Leland_Chee_Force_Collection.png|nolive=1}} — [[Leland Chee]] of the [[Lucasfilm Story Group]] has confirmed that [[in-universe]] information from ''[[Star Wars: Force Collection]]'' conforms with ''[[Star Wars]]'' [[canon]].</ref> The name originated in the [[Star Wars Legends|''Star Wars'' Legends]] continuity, where it was created by [[Louis J. Prosperi]] for the ''[[Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game]]'' supplement [[Wanted by Cracken (sourcebook)|''Wanted by Cracken'']], released by [[West End Games]] in [[1993]].<ref name="WBC">[[Wanted by Cracken (sourcebook)|''Wanted by Cracken'']]</ref>
